executivePulse.interpretation: The situation for memory and AI infrastructure remains tense. Enterprise SSDs, server DRAM / RDIMM and HBM are currently among the most strained areas. The Daily Check of 2026-08-17 reviewed eight relevant items; there is presently no confirmed material change in direction. New capacity and improved yields can relieve pressure but will reach the market only with delay. For buyers, supply assurance, alternative BOMs and early procurement remain decisive.

signals.title: Liquid Cooling Becomes Standard for High-End AI Infrastructure, with Penetration Expected to Reach 53% in 2026, Says TrendForce
signals.summary: Liquid cooling penetration among AI chips is projected to rise to 53% in 2026 and approach 60% in 2027. High-end chips from NVIDIA, AMD, and Google are driving the adoption of liquid cooling. NVIDIA’s rack-scale solution shipments are expected to double in 2026, while more than 80% of Google’s AI servers already use liquid cooling.
signals.analysis: This is relevant for datacentre storage: greater adoption of liquid cooling can change price dynamics, usable capacities and procurement strategies for enterprise SSDs.

signals.title: Samsung weighs Giheung R&D line for 2nm HBM foundry capacity
signals.summary: Aktuelle Meldung von digitimes: Samsung weighs Giheung R&D line for 2nm HBM foundry capacity
signals.analysis: HBM remains a central bottleneck for AI accelerators. Changes in production, qualification or demand will directly affect available GPU systems and pricing in the AI infrastructure market.

signals.title: Google, Amazon, and Meta All Just Raised Capex Guidance Again. This Boring Industrial Wins No Matter Whose AI Infrastructure Is Best.
signals.summary: Aktuelle Meldung von The Motley Fool: Google, Amazon, and Meta All Just Raised Capex Guidance Again. This Boring Industrial Wins No Matter Whose AI Infrastructure Is Best.
signals.analysis: Higher capex guidance alters the build‑out trajectory of AI and datacentre infrastructure. Increased productive compute capacity pulls server memory, enterprise storage, networking and power infrastructure along with it.
